title.narrative: Women Economic Strengthening and Resilience Project

description.narrative: Large rural areas in Zimbabwe are characterized by high levels of extreme poverty and have limited access to economic opportunities. In Mutoko, Mudzi, Goromonzi and Murehwa districts, many households rely on subsistence farming and small-scale agricultural activities for their livelihoods.Several factors constrain the potential for economic growth and income generation in these districts, including limited value chain development, financial exclusion, skills and knowledge gap, and gender disparities and social exclusion resulting in women and marginalized groups facing additional barriers to economic empowerment. Fortunately there are opportunities for improvement. With support of the Netherlands, this project seeks to make a tangible difference in the lives of women, youth, and the broader community by improving household income and contributing to the overall goal of eradicating extreme poverty in Mutoko, Mudzi, Murehwa and Goromonzi.The project will equip farmers with skills and knowledge necessary for increasing revenues from income-generating activities. By means of capacity building and establishing networks, participation in garlic, onion, beans and honey value chains will be promoted. Topics include technical trainings, business development and entrepreneurship, market intelligence, value addition and processing, and financial literacy. Proven approaches for establishing micro-loan groups and value chain-oriented groups will be introduced to facilitate access to finance and markets. All in all this project aims to uplift 1000 farmer households from extreme poverty.
